observations.why: First-person plural declarative enacts a decision as settled — authority of position or agreed process, not persuasion.
Quantified performance comparison argues from demonstrated capability — expert authority and rational-persuasion co-occur.
Stating a timeline as fact enacts scheduling authority without inviting consultation.
Labeling and categorizing the decision controls the factual frame — informational power via structuring what is known.
Categorizing the improvement as a labeled fact exercises informational control over how the decision is understood.
Labeling the schedule as a structured fact supplies and controls the informational frame around the migration.
